title: Being made to write right-handed at school
summary: Chicago teachers switched him to writing right-handed, unlike his school in New Orleans; he never stuttered.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, no, I don't write left-handed. That's the funny thing. When I went to school in Chicago, in those days, the teachers used to make you change hands. Now they don't do it with my kid. I mean, they say, if you left-handed, well, he's naturally left-handed like I was. And they don't change him. But when I come up here to school, the teachers changed me. I had started to write and left-handed because my first school was Fisk, and that was right around the corner from where I was living. And they closed the school because it was too near the district. Then they opened my McDonald 35 in Yarlins, and I went to McDonald. But down there, I mean, I started to write and left. But when I come up here to school, they start me going over. And now they don't do that to the kids. They say it's subject to retarded or something.
Yeah, sometimes it makes them stutter. Yeah. You never had any trouble, though, stuttering? No.
